findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data.

The bucket lacks an explicit ACL and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, leaving it potentially subject to default/public access settings and no protection against accidental public exposure.
The bucket storing ledger exports (likely financial data) has no server_side_encryption_configuration, meaning data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this sensitive bucket, so it could be misconfigured to allow public access without any guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No public access block configuration exists for this bucket, leaving it without protection against accidental public exposure.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so operational runbooks (potentially containing sensitive operational/security details) are unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured for this bucket, leaving it exposed to potential public access misconfiguration.

Although the audit trail bucket uses KMS encryption, it uses the 'log-delivery-write' ACL and has no explicit public access block, and lacks bucket policy restrictions, which could allow unintended write access beyond the intended logging service.

The object is uploaded to a bucket (reports_archive) that has no server-side encryption enabled, and no per-object server_side_encryption or kms_key_id parameter is specified, resulting in unencrypted storage of the vendor roster file, which may contain sensitive vendor data.
